name: Seated Arnold Press on Incline Bench
description: The incline-bench Arnold press performs the standard Arnold press rotation from supinated-to-pronated while seated on an incline bench (60-70 degrees), which provides a slight forward lean and greater back support than a vertical seated position. The incline alters the starting angle of the press, increasing anterior deltoid pre-stretch at the bottom and making the transition from the supinated starting position slightly more challenging through the mid-range.

execution.starting_position: Sit on a bench inclined to 60-70 degrees. Hold dumbbells in the Arnold press starting position — elbows bent, dumbbells at shoulder level, palms facing the body.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the bench high enough to be nearly vertical but not fully upright — this differentiates from a standard seated Arnold press.
steps: Step 1: Begin with dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing you, elbows forward.
Step 2: Begin pressing while simultaneously rotating the wrists outward.
Step 3: By the mid-point of the press, palms face forward (pronated).
Step 4: Continue pressing to full overhead extension.
Step 5: Lower while reversing the rotation — returning to the supinated position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the press. Inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Not completing the full rotation — the supination-to-pronation should be a full 180 degrees
Using too heavy a load — the rotation requires control
safety_considerations: The rotation combined with heavy loads increases wrist stress — moderate weight
Ensure the bench incline is stable and secure before loading
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Shoulder height supinated to full overhead extension pronated.
coaching_cues: Elbows go from forward to out as you press
Full rotation — 180 degrees of wrist turn
Drive the weight overhead — not just forward
